title: ACC Point Defense Battle Lab — counter-sUAS exercises & industry calls
agency: Air Combat Command, 319th Reconnaissance Wing, Grand Forks AFB ND
deadline: July 2026 call closed 07-31; exercises Aug & Dec 2026; final report to ACC/CC end-2026
fit_note: The call explicitly sought drone-on-drone interceptors to defend domestic Air Force and Space Force bases from Group 1-2 drones. This is UM's exact use case and an ideal first characterization venue. Watch for the next call.

title: DAF SBIR 26.BZ DAF26BZ01-DV001 Homeland Convoy Counter Drone Operations (Direct-to-Phase II)
fit_note: Homeland, public-road convoys; low-collateral kinetic allowed as a last resort; must be SOSA-compliant and integrate with the Medusa GRA. Similar topics recur — keep SOSA/MEDUSA integration on the roadmap.

title: Navy SBIR/STTR DON26BX03-NP002 — C-UAS Technology Development
amount: Phase I up to $200K base + $115K option
fit_note: Broad C-UAS topic (ATR, swarm detection, non-kinetic defeat). Navy CSO/BAA-style topics recur through the DSIP portal.

title: DoD SBIR/STTR Innovation Portal (DSIP) — rolling C-UAS topics
fit_note: Non-dilutive money and a sole-source Phase III path. Allen Control Systems' Army Bullfrog contract (topic A254-P030) shows SBIR to production in C-UAS. Set alerts for counter-UAS, interceptor, base defense, homeland.

title: UK MOD Project GOSHAWK / LCADE-LEAP next phase
deadline: GOSHAWK tender early 2026; LEAP production phase TBD
fit_note: UK-centric (UK SMEs favored). Possible later through a UK partner or AUKUS Pillar II channels.

title: Colombia National Anti-Drone Shield (~$1.6B)
type: International programme (US Commerce flagged as an export opportunity)
fit_note: Export path via the Commerce Dept Advocacy Center once UM has ITAR/EAR classification; interceptors are explicitly part of the architecture.

title: JIATF-401 C-UAS Marketplace (cuas.mil) vendor listing
type: Vendor vetting & listing (government buyers order directly)
amount: Access to DoD, DHS, DOJ, FBI and allied buyers
fit_note: Listing needs business verification, an export-control review and a product evaluation. Start the paperwork now (SAM.gov, CAGE, NIST 800-171 posture, export classification) so UM can list as soon as it has test data.
